response_text:
Great — below is a complete, family-focused Spring Break road‑trip plan (Seattle → San Antonio → Austin → Houston) that fits your timeline and target $3,000 total budget. I’ve given concrete hotel options, a kid-friendly day-by-day itinerary, driving stops, an estimated budget with savings tips, and practical advice for traveling with kids.

Quick trip summary
- Flights already booked: SEA → SAT arriving afternoon April 10; HOU → SEA departing morning April 18.
- Rental car pickup: SAT on April 10 (afternoon). Drop off: HOU (recommended) on April 17 evening (or morning of April 18 if you prefer; note extra hassle).
- Nights: San Antonio 3 nights (Apr 10–13), Austin 4 nights (Apr 13–17), Houston 1 night (Apr 17–18) — I recommend a Houston night because of the early flight.
- Total family: 2 adults + kids (8 & 11).

1) Rental car — recommendation, price estimate & tips
Recommended category
- Mid‑size SUV (compact or mid-size crossover such as Toyota RAV4 / Honda CR‑V / similar).
  - Why: more space for luggage and snacks, comfortable for 2–4+ hour drives, decent fuel economy, fits booster seat(s) and strollers if you bring them.
  - If you want to save money and don’t need extra cargo: a midsize sedan will save $100–200.

Estimated cost (7–8 days, one‑way SAT → HOU)
- Ballpark: $550–$800 total. Use $650 as a working estimate that includes base rate + taxes + one‑way drop fee.
- Notes: One‑way drop fees vary widely by company/location (roughly $100–$300). Prepay / book early to lock rates.

Practical rental tips (to save money and avoid surprises)
- Book early and compare aggregator sites (Kayak, Rentalcars.com, Expedia) and direct (Avis, Hertz, Enterprise) — sometimes direct gives better loyalty perks.
- Use any corporate/AAA/membership discounts or code on your credit card.
- Check if your credit card includes collision damage waiver (CDW) — that lets you decline daily insurance add‑ons.
- Bring your child booster seat(s) if possible — rental seats cost ~$10–15/day and may not be as clean.
- Choose “full-to-full” fuel policy to save money vs prepay refuel options.
- Inspect & photograph the car at pickup (take photos of all sides and odometer).
- If you can drop at HOU instead of IAH (and your flight is HOU), pick HOU to save airport-to-airport logistics.

2) Hotels (family-friendly options)

San Antonio (3 nights: Apr 10–13) — near River Walk
1. Drury Plaza Hotel San Antonio Riverwalk
   - Approx price: $150–200/night
   - Pros: Free hot breakfast + evening “kickback” snacks, indoor/outdoor pool, great Riverwalk location, suites available.
   - Cons: Can be busy; river views depend on room.
   - Family fit: Free breakfast + snacks = big savings; pool + suites great for kids.

2. Hotel Contessa (a luxury all‑suite on the Riverwalk)
   - Approx price: $200–320/night
   - Pros: All suites with kitchenettes, riverfront, pool, steps to attractions.
   - Cons: Pricier.
   - Family fit: Suite layout and kitchenette make meals easier with kids.

3. Hyatt Regency San Antonio Riverwalk (or Hilton Palacio del Rio)
   - Approx price: $180–300/night
   - Pros: Central to the Alamo, boat tours, large rooms, pool.
   - Cons: Higher tourist traffic, parking fees may apply.
   - Family fit: Good central base for short walks to most attractions.

Austin (4 nights: Apr 13–17) — walkable to South Congress or downtown
1. Hotel San Jose (SoCo)
   - Approx price: $200–300/night
   - Pros: Right on South Congress, cool courtyard, pool, casual vibe.
   - Cons: Boutique rooms smaller; fewer family conveniences.
   - Family fit: Walkable to shops and food trucks — fun, local vibe.

2. South Congress Hotel (upscale SoCo)
   - Approx price: $300–450/night
   - Pros: Excellent SoCo location, pools, restaurants on site.
   - Cons: Expensive.
   - Family fit: Great location and amenities if budget allows.

3. Hyatt Place Austin Downtown / Hampton Inn Austin Downtown
   - Approx price: $150–225/night
   - Pros: Family rooms, free breakfast (Hampton/Hyatt Place), closer to Lady Bird Lake and Congress Ave — walkable to downtown, easy access to SoCo by short drive/ride.
   - Cons: Slightly farther from SoCo than the boutiques (10–25 minute walk or short drive).
   - Family fit: Value pick with free breakfast & larger rooms.

(If you want walkability to SoCo for most of the stay, prefer Hotel San Jose or Austin Motel; for savings or free breakfast choose Hyatt Place/Hampton downtown and take a short ride to SoCo.)

If you prefer IAH vs HOU drop-off
- You may want one night in Houston near HOU (if flying HOU) — budget hotels near Hobby (HOU) = $100–140/night with shuttle service.

3) Day‑by‑day itinerary (kid‑friendly, 8 & 11)

San Antonio (April 10–13)
April 10 — Arrival afternoon
- Pick up rental at SAT (allow 45–60 min after arrival).
- Drive ~15–20 min to Riverwalk hotel; check in and let kids rest (short nap).
- Easy evening: stroll the River Walk, casual dinner (family style Tex‑Mex), short river barge boat tour if kids are still awake (30–45 min).
- Early bed to recover from travel + time change.

April 11 — Full day (kid favorites)
- Morning: The DoSeum (San Antonio’s children’s museum) — hands‑on play & exhibits (2–3 hours).
- Lunch: nearby family restaurant or grab sandwiches.
- Afternoon: San Antonio Zoo (Brackenridge Park) OR Witte Museum if you prefer natural history (2–3 hours).
- Evening: Dinner at Riverwalk; consider ice cream and a relaxed stroll.

April 12 — Full day (cave/adventure or theme park)
Option A — Natural Bridge Caverns & Wildlife/Adventure
- Morning: Drive ~25 min to Natural Bridge Caverns — Discovery Tour, ropes/Canopy Challenge or gem mining. Great for active kids.
- Afternoon: Drive-through Natural Bridge Wildlife Ranch (safari) OR return to Riverwalk for free time.
Option B — Theme park day
- SeaWorld OR Six Flags Fiesta Texas (seasonal) — full‑day option if your family prefers rides and shows.
- Dinner near the hotel; relax by hotel pool.

April 13 — Morning + drive to Austin
- Quick morning: Alamo visit (short 30–45 min) and one last River Walk stroll.
- Grab lunch (or picnic) and head north on I‑35 to Austin (~1.5 hours).
- Possible stop en route: San Marcos (outlet mall / Wonder World Cave) or Gruene / New Braunfels (walk Gruene Historic District).
- Arrive Austin late afternoon; check in near SoCo/downtown.
- Evening: South Congress stroll, dinner, ice cream; if time & season, watch Congress Ave bat emergence at dusk (free and fun for kids).

Austin (April 13–17)
April 14 — Full day (hands‑on + park)
- Morning: Thinkery (Austin children’s museum) — especially great for ages 8–11 (2–3 hours).
- Lunch near Zilker area.
- Afternoon: Zilker Park — playground, Zilker Zephyr miniature train, and if weather is warm, Barton Springs (swim) or splash at adjacent pool.
- Evening: casual dinner, early night or live music that’s family-friendly.

April 15 — Day trip / nature (pick one)
Option A — Enchanted Rock (1.5 hr each way) — hike and wildflower viewing (seasonal). Good active day outside.
Option B — Fredericksburg & Wildseed Farms (drive ~1.25–1.5 hours) — scenic, kid‑friendly farming and flower fields, plus a slower day exploring small towns.
Option C — Inner Space Cavern (San Marcos) — guided cave tour (closer than Enchanted Rock).

April 16 — Downtown & lake fun
- Morning: Bullock Texas State History Museum or Austin Nature & Science Center (free) for kid-friendly exhibits.
- Lunch downtown or food trucks.
- Afternoon: Kayak/paddleboat rental on Lady Bird Lake (family rentals available) or rent bikes for a lakeside ride.
- Evening: If you didn’t see bats earlier, try Congress Ave bridge at dusk today — a cool natural spectacle.

April 17 — Morning checkout, drive to Houston
- Pack and depart Austin mid‑morning to avoid Austin PM traffic.
- Drive to Houston (I‑10E / US‑290 route) ~2.5–3 hrs depending on traffic.
- Optional stop: Brenham (Blue Bell Creamery tour — detour), Bastrop State Park (stretch), or a BBQ stop in Lockhart (if you like BBQ).
- Arrive HOU late afternoon; return rental car at airport; check into nearby hotel for early flight next morning.

April 18 — Early flight from HOU → SEA
- Airport shuttle from hotel → HOU, and fly home.

4) Top 5 kid‑friendly must‑do’s (ages 8–11)

San Antonio
1. The DoSeum — interactive children’s museum (science, creativity).
2. San Antonio River Walk boat tour — relaxing, easy intro to the city.
3. San Antonio Zoo — large zoo with lots of exhibits.
4. Natural Bridge Caverns (or Natural Bridge Wildlife Ranch) — caves, ropes, and drive‑thru safari.
5. The Alamo & Missions (short, guided visit) or a theme park (Six Flags/SeaWorld) if your kids prefer rides.

Austin
1. Thinkery — Austin’s children’s museum (hands-on activities).
2. Zilker Park + Zilker Zephyr & Barton Springs (park + splash/swim).
3. Lady Bird Lake — family paddleboat/kayak.
4. Congress Avenue Bridge bats at dusk (seasonal and crowd‑pleasing).
5. Bullock Texas State History Museum or Austin Nature & Science Center — both great for curious kids.

5) Driving routes & recommended stops

SAT → Austin
- Best route: I‑35 North (direct, ~80–85 miles).
- Drive time: about 1.5–2 hours depending on traffic.
- Good stops:
  - New Braunfels / Gruene Historic District (short detour) — cute riverfront shops, maybe grab a snack.
  - San Marcos — outlet malls, Wonder World Cave (kid cave tours).
  - Lockhart (if you want famous Texas BBQ; plan for time).

Austin → Houston (to HOU)
- Best route: I‑10 East is the most direct from Austin area; from central Austin you may pick TX‑71 to I‑10 depending on your start point. Expect ~165–175 miles.
- Drive time: ~2.5–3 hours (plan extra time for traffic around Austin & approaching Houston).
- Good stops:
  - Bastrop State Park (stretch legs and a short hike).
  - Brenham / Blue Bell Creamery (detour north on US‑290) — kids love ice cream tours.
  - Rest stops & major gas stations — plan fuel before long stretches; there are plentiful gas stations on I‑10.

Fuel & breaks
- Expect roughly 300–500 total driving miles; plan fuel stop(s) in San Marcos or Bastrop depending on route. Top up before long legs to avoid running low.

6) Budget breakdown (estimated)
Below is a mid‑budget plan with realistic, family‑friendly choices. These are estimates — book early to lock rates.

| Category                          | Estimated Cost |
|-----------------------------------|----------------|
| Rental car (7–8 days, mid‑size SUV, one‑way incl. fees) | $650 |
| San Antonio hotels (3 nights)     | $540 |
| Austin hotels (4 nights)          | $700 |
| Houston hotel (1 night near HOU)  | $120 |
| Activities/tickets (family)       | $300 |
| Food/dining (8 days, family)      | $520 |
| Gas                               | $120 |
| --------------------------------- | ------ |
| Total                             | $2,950 |

Notes & where to cut costs if needed
- This estimate is under your $3,000 budget but leaves little wiggle room for unexpected fees (parking, tolls, extra rental insurance, special attraction add‑ons).
- If you need to trim:
  - Save on hotels: pick one or two nights in economy hotels with free breakfast (saves $100–300).
  - Car: choose a compact sedan instead of mid‑size SUV (~$50–150 savings).
  - Food: use hotel breakfasts, occasional grocery store picnics, and limit pricier dinners.
  - Activities: skip a theme park (SeaWorld / Six Flags) and choose free parks and museums.
- Watch for hotel parking charges (downtown hotels often charge $15–40/day). Choose hotels with free parking when possible.

7) Practical tips (apps, packing, April specifics)

Best apps
- Navigation: Google Maps or Waze (real‑time traffic).
- Trip planning & stops: Roadtrippers (plan interesting stops), AllTrails (hikes).
- Dining: Yelp / OpenTable (family seating/reservations), Tripadvisor.
- Tickets/events: official attraction sites for prebooking; Eventbrite/local city calendar for festivals.
- Kids entertainment: Audible (audiobooks), Spotify (kids playlists), Netflix/YouTube downloads.

What to pack in the car
- Reusable water bottles + cooler with drinks/snacks (sandwiches, fruit, granola bars).
- Booster seat (bring your own to save rental cost) — TX law: children under 8 must use booster unless 4'9" or taller.
- Wet wipes, paper towels, trash bags.
- Small first aid kit, motion sickness meds if needed.
- Portable charger + charging cables and a phone mount for navigation.
- Blankets/pillows for naps; travel games, coloring books, headphones for kids.
- Swimsuits and quick‑dry towels (many hotels have pools).
- Sunscreen, hats, comfortable walking shoes.

April‑specific notes & events
- Fiesta San Antonio is usually in April (mid‑April most years) — large civic festival events can increase crowds and hotel rates. Check the official Fiesta schedule; if your dates overlap, book/ticket attractions early.
- Wildflower (bluebonnet) season across Texas typically peaks March–April — gorgeous pink fields in the Hill Country between San Antonio and Austin (consider Fredericksburg or Enchanted Rock photo stops).
- Weather in April: generally mild to warm (daytime 60s–80s F) but can have sudden showers. Pack layers and light rain jackets.
- Congress Ave bat season: bats are present March–October; their emergence is best at dusk. It’s free but can draw crowds — show up early.

Final quick checklist & recommended bookings
- Book rental car now (lock in one‑way fee). Confirm child seat needs or bring boosters.
- Reserve The DoSeum and Thinkery online (these can have timed entry).
- If you prefer theme parks (SeaWorld / Six Flags), buy tickets online for discounts and skip-the-line.
- Choose hotels with free breakfast and pool if possible — big savings and kid entertainment.
- Plan one scenic day in Hill Country (Enchanted Rock or Fredericksburg) if your family likes hiking & wildflowers.
